column1: # *** HOW THE LINES DO AND DO NOT JOIN (the table on /lines/, and the bridges in its drawing). 27 October 2026. ***
# One row per join this archive has a verdict on: between two lanes, or between a lane and a household or a person. Written by
# hand, in the archive's own words, from the page or the register note that states it (the `href`). A verdict is research: no tool
# writes or changes one. Where the archive's data does not say whether two lines join, there is NO ROW: the question is listed for
# David instead (it is not this file's to answer).
# a, b     lane:<key> (data/lerena-lines.tsv) | row:<who> (a household of data/lerena-lines-unplaced.tsv) |
#          person:<slug>[|<the words to print>] | text:<words> (for a side that is not one line, e.g. every lane)
# status   documented  the join rests on a document, read            -> printed; the two are one family
#          candidate   proposed on evidence short of a document      -> printed, and drawn as the kit's bridge (lane to lane, or lane to household)
#          refused     tested, and the archive says it is false      -> printed
#          open        the archive says in so many words that it does not know -> printed
# label    the few words drawn beside a bridge (a candidate only)
# says     what the archive says, and why
a
column5: says

column1: lane:sancho
column4: Hypothesis 1c: a Montevideo house, and no paper joins it to Juan Carlos
column5: Hypothesis 1c, that the family came from Uruguay, not Argentina. For it: the Rosario baptism index, read end to end for 1731-1901, holds one Lerena, and he is a Lerena Lenguas of this house; and in the army drawer Cajon 985 every traceable father of a Lerena card is a Uruguayan family's son. Against it: no link has been shown between Luis Lerena Lenguas and Juan Carlos Lerena, and Juan Carlos is in none of the household's children. The story draws the break at Sancho's grandchildren and leaves it open.

column1: lane:direct
column5: Pablo Armando Lerena married Mary Septima Taylor at St Dominic's, Wynberg, on 3 September 1911: entry 160 of the duplicate original register. The Taylor line is drawn as a lane of its own because this archive keeps it as one; the two meet at that act, and their children are counted on the direct line.

column1: person:don-luis-lerena-probably-luis-lerena-y-fernandez|The house of Luis Lerena and Justiniana Lenguas
column5: Three acts name Luis Lerena's parents as Sancho and Maria Fernandez: his own baptism of 10 February 1811, his second marriage of 3 March 1842 and his son Alberto Octavio's baptism of 7 October 1850. So the Lerena Lenguas household, Gilberto of the Argentine Stud Book among them, is Sancho's grandchildren. (The register's own link from Luis to Sancho is still marked as resting on a tree, and his row still says 'probably'.)

column1: person:zelmira-carlota-lerena-larriera|The Lerena Larriera of San Jose
column5: Set aside as 'not ours' on 14 September 2026 and retracted on 21 September: Alberto Lerena's Montevideo death registration of 2 March 1921, read at the image, names his parents as Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel. The nine children of Alberto and Maria Ines Larriera are great-grandchildren of Sancho. A refusal the archive itself withdrew.

column1: person:bernabe-lerena|The Trinidad kindred, Alejandro's house
column5: The Trinidad expedientes of 1855 and 1858 name Alejandro Lerena and Margarita Fernandez as the parents of Socorro and Bernabe, and Ramon Lerena and Maria Gonzalez as their grandparents; Alejandro's own marriage of 16 September 1825, read at the plate, calls him the son of Ramon Lerena and Maria Josefa Gonzalez. Ramon of Rosario-Colla is Ramon of the Trinidad diagram.

column1: person:cipriano-lerena|The house of Cipriano Lerena and Lauriana Beloqui
column5: Held apart from the Colla house until 9 October 2026. The Flores birth act of his daughter Carmen Donata, 2 March 1895, has him name his wife and both his parents, Mauricio and Casimira Montano: so the Beloqui children are grandchildren of Mauricio of Colla. (The register does not yet draw his link to Mauricio; the line counts him by this act.)

column1: lane:ramon
column5: Whether the Trinidad kindred joins Sancho's house is an open question with no evidence either way, which is why no join is drawn between them.

column1: lane:arturo
column5: On 13 September 2026 an Arturo Lerena born at Montevideo in 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel, was run together with the Arturo Lerena of the army drawer. That was two men: the Uruguayan record gives that Arturo's wife as Ema Regules, and the Arturo of the drawer married Amalia Diaz and had children in La Pampa, Mendoza and Entre Rios. The row was withdrawn the same evening.

column1: person:juan-carlos-gonzalez-lerena|Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena (married 1922)
column5: The only 'Juan Carlos Lerena' in FamilySearch's full text besides a 2001 death, checked and excluded on 15 September 2026: Lerena is his second surname, his mother's, and he married in 1922. Pablo Armando's father must carry Lerena as his father's name and have been born by about the 1850s. He stands on Ramon's line, by his mother.

column1: row:LERINA
column5: Hypothesis 1b, that the family was Italian and the name nearer LERINA: the four LERINA arrivals of 1889 remain excluded, on their dates and not on a judgement about the surname. The eldest was fifty-nine and the youngest seventeen when they landed, seven years after Pablo Armando was born.

column1: row:LARENA of Cayasta
column5: Retracted: Cayasta was an Italian colony, and its 'Larena' is almost certainly an Italian surname mis-rendered; the apparent cluster is a transcription artefact. At Gualeguaychu the spelling is sometimes this family's.

column1: person:mauricio-lerena-2|Mauricio Lerena of Flores (born about 1836)
column5: He is not the man who married at San Jose in 1837: fifty in 1886 is a birth about 1836, and the other Mauricio married in February 1837. Whether he is that man's son is carried, not resolved.

column1: row:GILBERTO LERENA, Argentine, born 1879
column4: the 1928 arrival may be Gilberto Lerena Salvanach
column5: An Argentine Gilberto Lerena, born 1879, landed at Buenos Aires in 1928 with a son Gilberto of twelve. What fits Gilberto Lerena Salvanach, the Stud Book Gilberto's eldest son: a birth year one out, Argentine nationality, Buenos Aires, a marriage of 1906. Deliberately not merged: both rows are index-level, and the Argentine military record or the CEMLA entry would settle it.

column1: row:JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA
column5: The two named as Pablo Armando's parents on his army card of 1908 appear in no other record anywhere. Every lane above is a candidate and none has been shown to hold them.

column1: row:GIL LERENA and ANASTASIA SANTA CRUZ
column5: He is not placed: no act names his parents, and nothing ties him to Alejandro's brothers or to Sancho's sons.

column1: row:CARLOS LERENA of Mendoza
column5: The forename AVELINO, which his son carries, is the one that runs through Sancho's house: suggestive, and not evidence. Worked in September and not joined.

column1: row:PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA and TERESA LEONARD
column5: His father could be Pedro Antonio, son of Sancho, only if that man married a second wife, Maria Pereyra, after Vicenta Vega, which nothing says.

column1: row:MAURICIO LERENA and PETRONA AGUILAR
column5: He may be the Mauricio of Flores born about 1836, and he is not the Colla Mauricio, who had a wife Casimira. Not merged.

column1: row:The LARENA of Gualeguaychu
column5: What is missing is any document joining them to a Uruguayan house.

column1: row:The LERENA of Trinidad with no father named
column5: Real people on real acts, attached to nobody.

column1: row:PEDRO LERENA and JUANA CAMACHO
column2: text:any line, or any other stock
column5: This archive cannot yet tell which stock he belongs to, which is itself the finding: an Italian-born Lerena in the department this archive rests an 1846 couple on.

column1: row:LEANDRO LERENA and LUCIA LLANOS
column5: A fourth Spanish arrival beside the three the Spain lane already draws, and not shown to be connected to any of them. Segovia is outside the one Spanish cluster this archive can point to, La Rioja, which makes kinship with the Navarrete household less likely, not more.

column1: row:The LERENA y LERENA of Navarrete
column5: Spanish subjects out of Logrono, kept apart on purpose: no connection is claimed between this household and any of the lines.
